correctness.rationale: Pick-Ehrhart and coefficient inversion yield the stated universal quartic. Seven exact finite polynomial certificates have nonnegative coefficients, with 784, 36, 36, 75, 25, 6, and 3 terms, all strictly positive. The quartic has a negative test value and a positive discriminant, forcing four simple real roots. Cubic and quadratic boundary strata have strictly positive discriminants; positive coefficients exclude nonnegative roots. All symbolic identities and certificate rows have been regenerated from the accompanying code.

originality.rationale: The published product-preservation theorem applies when both factor Ehrhart numerators are real rooted. Primitive-edge lattice triangles with one, two, or three interior lattice points have non-real-rooted numerators, yet the new assertion covers their product with every lattice polygon and proves simplicity. Published Hadamard-product log-concavity and large-width results do not imply the exceptional cases. No identical or stronger covered statement was located in the inspected full primary sections and semantic published-record checks; residual priority risk is recorded.
residual_risks: Historical priority may be subsumed by an unindexed Segre-product theorem stated in different terminology.
The polynomial positivity certificate is exact and reproducible but has not received an independent scientific audit.

value.rationale: A complete classification in a natural four-dimensional product class removes precisely three exceptional lattice-triangle input types not supplied by the known conditional real-rootedness theorem. The result forces strict simple negative roots for all counterparts, and supplies an explicit universally valid quartic formula. This is a motivated structural strengthening of contemporary Ehrhart-product preservation results rather than an arbitrary table entry.
